newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB details 1997/98 wheat, barley prices by grade.
newsitem.headline: CWB details 1997/98 wheat, barley prices by grade.

text.p: Canadian Wheat Board on Thursday issued a detailed breakdown of government-backed initial partial payments for all grades of wheat, durum, feed and malt barley for the 1997/98 (Aug/July) crop year.
Initial prices are government-backed first-payment prices of 70 to 80 percent of the CWB's estimate of world grain prices.

Discounts for tough and damp grain increased C$1 a tonne compared to 1996/97 (Aug/July) crop year, the CWB said. Tough discounts will be C$8 a tonne for wheat, C$7 for barley. Damp discounts will be C$15.50 for wheat, C$13.50 for barley.

Initial payments for wheat fell from August 1996 due to larger world wheat supplies. World output, including durum wheat, was forecast to reach 587 million tonnes, the second highest on record, the CWB said.
The record was 588 million tonnes in 1990/91.
U.S. output was forecast to increase four million tonnes to 66.2 million tonnes, due mainly to favorable hard red winter wheat yields.
Early indications from the U.S. hard red winter harvest were that protein levels were lower than last year, suggesting the possibility of higher protein premiums.
Protein premiums, however, will also depend on spring wheat quality in the U.S. and Canada.
Increased ending stocks from 1996/97 compared to the year before along with large forecast production were expected to increase world ending stocks to 120 million tonnes in 1997/98.

Initial payments for durum wheat were slightly higher than August 1996 due to tighter world supplies. The U.S., European Union and Canada were expected to havest smaller crops in 1997/98 compared to 1996/97 while drought cut output among the major importers in North Africa. Ending stocks in durum in 1997/98 should be 3.6 million tonnes versus 3.8 million.
Feed barley values were affected by overall world coarse grain output which was forecast to reach 898 million tonnes in 1997/98 compared to 872 million tonnes in 1996/97.

Larger carry-in stocks should raise total supply to 1.018 billion tonnes compare to last year's 997 million tonnes and the U.S. corn crop was near record levels with output expected at 246 million tonnes, second only to 1994's crop of 257 million.

Malting barley values should be affected by total barley supplies as well as the proportion of the crop that is deemed to be of malting quality. Global barley quality will be an important factor in determining prices, the CWB said.
Initial payments in Canadian dollars per tonne based on grain in store St. Lawrence or Vancouver:
CWRS=Canada Western Spring Wheat. CPSR=Canada Prairie Spring Red. CPSW=Canada Prairie Spring White. CWRW= Canada Western Red Winter. CWES=Canada Western Extra Strong.
CWSWS=Canada Western Soft White Spring. CWF=Canada Western Feed. CWAD=Canada Western Amber Durum. CW=Canada Western.
